findings.title: A backup code can authenticate without the account password
findings.description:
Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is nonempty. The new backup-code branch then accepts a valid backup code without validating that TOTP value. Consequently, submitting a valid backup code together with an arbitrary nonempty `totpCode` bypasses password verification.

Enforce first-factor verification independently of client-supplied second-factor fields. If external-provider authentication needs a separate path, require verified server-side proof of that authentication rather than using the presence of `totpCode`.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic
findings.description:
The code checks a previously read encrypted array and then updates the user by ID alone. Two concurrent requests can read the same unused code, both validate it, and both successfully authenticate. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other’s changes, restoring a consumed code.

Consume codes atomically—for example, with a conditional update matching the previously read ciphertext and rejecting unsuccessful updates, or with separately stored code records consumed transactionally. Add concurrency tests verifying that exactly one request can redeem a code.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-code dialog leaves the security status stale
findings.description:
After the enable endpoint succeeds, the component only changes the displayed step. The parent’s `onEnable` callback, which invalidates `viewer.me`, runs only when the explicit backup-codes Close button is clicked.

The dialog still permits dismissal through Escape or an outside click via the unchanged `onOpenChange` handler. Taking either route leaves the settings switch displaying disabled even though two-factor authentication is enabled on the server. Synchronize the parent state immediately after successful enablement, independently of how the backup-code dialog closes.

findings.title: Copy confirmation is shown before recovery codes reach the clipboard
findings.description:
`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` returns a promise, but the handler neither awaits it nor handles rejection before displaying a success toast. If clipboard access is denied, users receive confirmation that their recovery codes were copied when they were not, potentially leaving them without a saved recovery method.

Await the write, show success only after fulfillment, and provide an actionable error or download fallback when clipboard access fails or is unavailable.

findings.title: Password visibility is no longer keyboard-accessible
findings.description:
Adding `tabIndex={-1}` removes the password-visibility button from sequential keyboard navigation across every `PasswordField`. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach and activate this control normally.

Keep the button keyboard-focusable. If this change is intended to control initial modal focus, configure focus at the modal level rather than removing a shared interactive control from the tab order.
